title: EU’s top AI adviser urges commissioners to use the technology to fix bloc’s economy
content:
BRUSSELS — The EU should focus less on winning the race to build artificial intelligence and more on how to deploy it to turn around the bloc’s sluggish productivity, the European Commission’s chief AI adviser told commissioners.

The technology is Europe’s best chance to accelerate growth in a range of sectors — including health, agriculture, transport, defense and manufacturing — Jim Hagemann Snabe, the EU’s new special envoy for industrial AI, told the bloc’s 27 commissioners at a Sept. 4 seminar, according to two Commission officials. They were granted anonymity to discuss the private briefing.

The EU is trying to capture the economic gains of rapidly advancing AI even as it grapples with the technology’s risks to jobs, security and society. Europe’s leaders should not worry too much about leading the development of frontier AI models, but should “be the ones who draw the greatest value from it” while managing its dangers, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said in her State of the Union speech last week.
snippet: BRUSSELS — The EU should focus less on winning the race to build artificial intelligence and more on how to deploy it to turn around the bloc’s sluggish productivity, the European Commission’s chief
creator: Zoya Sheftalovich

title: Peter Thiel slams pope’s AI encyclical as gift to Chinese Communist Party
content:
Tech billionaire and artificial intelligence investor Peter Thiel criticized Pope Leo XIV on Thursday, accusing the pontiff of serving as a “useful idiot for the [Chinese Communist Party]” by calling on world leaders to regulate AI.

During an interview with Mathias Döpfner, CEO of POLITICO’s parent company Axel Springer, the PayPal co-founder said the pope’s May encyclical would do nothing to rein in China’s AI ambitions — but could cause the U.S. and its allies to place onerous rules on the technology.

“The Communist Party of China is not going to listen to the pope,” Thiel told Döpfner, “There’s a chance people in the U.S. will. And so in effect, the Pope’s encyclical was working for the Communist party.”

“I’m not saying he was an agent of the communists, but he was at least acting as a useful idiot for the CCP,” Thiel added.

Spokespeople for the Vatican did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

title: EU Parliament president urges Germany to do deal in US drug pricing dispute
content:
NEW YORK — The president of the European Parliament, Roberta Metsola, says Germany should seek a deal with the Trump administration to resolve their trade dispute over drug pricing.

“If you don’t talk directly and reach a deal — the art of the deal — then the consequences might be more difficult to swallow. So my advice to anyone would be: Just try to find it,” she said in an exclusive interview with POLITICO on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative is currently investigating Germany’s drug pricing policies, accusing it of “persistent underpayment” for pharmaceutical products.

In a hearing this week in Washington, a clear majority of witnesses supported this claim. The investigation could ultimately provide the legal justification for Trump to impose new tariffs on German exports.

Metsola advocated for a compromise between Washington and Berlin to avoid “an impossible race on drugs.” Europe could “still lead in pharmaceuticals,” she said. But the bloc has to become “much more agile, not only in pricing but also in terms of clinical trials and bringing new products on the market.”
snippet: NEW YORK — The president of the European Parliament, Roberta Metsola, says Germany should seek a deal with the Trump administration to resolve their trade dispute over drug pricing.
creator: Stefanie Bolzen

title: White House asks OpenAI and Anthropic to hold new models from UK testers until US review
content:
The White House has asked OpenAI and Anthropic not to share their new artificial intelligence models with the U.K. government’s testing agency until the models have gone through testing with the U.S. government, according to a person familiar with the matter and a senior U.S. administration official, both of whom were granted anonymity to describe the request.

The request, which came from the Office of the National Cyber Director, puts companies in the difficult position of having to choose between withholding their models from U.K.’s AI Security Institute – one of the most well-resourced government testing agencies in the world which previously enjoyed privileged early access to models – or risk upsetting the Trump White House. The senior administration official said the White House wants the U.S. to review the models and take steps to make sure U.S. systems are secure before the models are shared with U.S. partners.

“Because they’re American companies and this has been our policy with every new frontier model that comes out,” the senior official explained.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
snippet: The White House has asked OpenAI and Anthropic not to share their new artificial intelligence models with the U.K. government’s testing agency until the models have gone through testing with the U.S.
creator: Sophia Cai, Joseph Bambridge

title: Von der Leyen ally slams EU Commission’s AI response
content:
The European Commission has failed to keep pace with AI developments, Axel Voss, a key German conservative lawmaker on tech policy, said in an interview.

An EPP ally of Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in the European Parliament, Voss criticized the way the Commission is enforcing its artificial intelligence rules in the wake of a series of AI hacking incidents, including OpenAI-powered agents going rogue and breaking into the AI company Hugging Face.

“The whole working method of the European Commission is not adapted to these extremely fast-changing … developments,” he said during a POLITICO podcast interview that goes live Friday.

The enforcement of the EU’s 2024 AI Act, which mandates that companies take measures to avoid losing control of their models, “is not on the level [where] we would like to have it,” he added.

The comments shine the spotlight on the European Commission’s Artificial Intelligence Office, which was put in charge of enforcing the AI Act in August.

Voss also said the Commission’s overall response to the fast pace of technological developments is lagging, singling out von der Leyen’s State of the Union last week.
snippet: The European Commission has failed to keep pace with AI developments, Axel Voss, a key German conservative lawmaker on tech policy, said in an interview.
creator: Pieter Haeck, Anne McElvoy

title: US, Chinese visions for AI regulation differ sharply at UN meeting
content:
Top officials from the U.S. and China on Wednesday promoted starkly conflicting visions for international AI safety, with the Americans arguing against expanded regulation while Beijing signaled an openness to restrictions on the technology.

The opposing world views — laid out during a United Nations General Assembly Security Council meeting — made clear that building an international consensus on the rapidly-evolving technology could be very challenging.

White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios strenuously opposed creating new global governance for controlling AI development.

“The United States totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme of control of superintelligence,” Kratsios said, quoting a line from President Donald Trump’s speech to the UNGA on Tuesday.

While Kratsios told the council that the U.S. is “committed to diplomacy and dialogue,” he stressed that countries should “preserve national sovereignty” on governing AI rather than “abdicate responsibility to international bodies.”

But China’s U.N. representative Fu Cong appealed for closer global collaboration on AI safeguards.

title: Cybercriminal group claims to steal thousands of FBI employee records
content:
The FBI said it is investigating a possible breach into its online jobs portal, after a prolific cybercrime group publicly claimed to have stolen personal information of FBI personnel.

“The FBI is aware of claims regarding unauthorized activity affecting FBIjobs.gov and is currently investigating,” the FBI National Press Office said in a statement.

Confirmation of an ongoing investigation came hours after a cybercriminal group known as ShinyHunters posted a message online claiming it had stolen “very sensitive” data on “almost all” FBI agents, as well as those who had applied for jobs at the bureau.

The group provided a sample of stolen data affecting 5,000 supposed FBI agents to 404 Media, which first reported on the alleged hack. The sample data set included agent names, home addresses, phone numbers and information on agents’ spouses, the outlet said.
snippet: The FBI said it is investigating a possible breach into its online jobs portal, after a prolific cybercrime group publicly claimed to have stolen personal information of FBI personnel.
creator: John Sakellariadis, Maggie Miller, Elleiana Green

title: AI anxiety is sweeping the globe — and cutting across party lines
content:
The freakout over artificial intelligence that started in Silicon Valley and led to growing American calls to pause development has swept Western countries.

A new POLITICO Poll finds that pluralities of adults in the U.S., Canada and Europe want to pause AI development regardless of their political leanings — and most believe there’s a real risk the technology could destroy humanity.

Pluralities of respondents in several countries say it’s ok for their country to fall behind others in the development of AI if it means being more responsible and secure when advancing it. And they’re more likely to expect AI will destroy jobs rather than create them. 

This is coming as world leaders are gathering in New York for the United Nations General Assembly and grappling with how to regulate the technology — or not.
snippet: The freakout over artificial intelligence that started in Silicon Valley and led to growing American calls to pause development has swept Western countries.
creator: Tyler Katzenberger, Pieter Haeck

title: EU and Canada to unveil new partnership, but it may not be ‘associate membership,’ says ambassador
content:
Ottawa and Brussels will announce a comprehensive set of partnerships within the coming year, but the shape of the future relationship is still up for discussion, Canada’s ambassador to the EU said Tuesday.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced during her State of the Union speech last week that the door would be open to Canada becoming “the first associate member” of the EU. But Ottawa has played down the formal nature of that arrangement.

“It was enormously gratifying for Canada to hear that from the president because I think it reflects the fact that Europeans see Canada in the same way that we see Europe,” Jonathan Wilkinson told POLITICO’s Brussels Playbook Live Summit.

“Ultimately, I’m less fussed about what we end up calling it. I’m more fussed about that we have initiatives that are really going to drive prosperity, economic security, and a range of things moving forward,” he said.
snippet: Ottawa and Brussels will announce a comprehensive set of partnerships within the coming year, but the shape of the future relationship is still up for discussion, Canada’s ambassador to the EU said
creator: Sarah Wheaton, Gabriel Gavin

title: Trump rejects global entity for AI oversight
content:
President Donald Trump condemned the idea of a global entity to oversee artificial intelligence in his remarks at the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday.

He said the United States “rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control” AI, just a day ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s arrival at the White House for meetings, in which AI could be a major topic of discussion.

The president insisted in his remarks that the U.S. is leading the world in AI innovation and reiterated his argument that the technology’s disruptive or possibly dangerous capabilities are a “hoax.” It comes as Trump has warned that efforts to regulate AI could hamper American efforts and allow China to get ahead.

“We’re leading now over China by a lot and everyone else and we’re going to keep it that way. We’re going to keep it very, very straight and very strong. I’m not going to stifle growth of anything that’s going to be bigger than the industrial revolution,” Trump said. “We will be very careful and that’s why we have a Department of Justice.”

The president also said the name should be changed to “super intelligence,” calling on other nations to drop the use of “artificial.”
snippet: President Donald Trump condemned the idea of a global entity to oversee artificial intelligence in his remarks at the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday.
creator: Alex Gangitano

title: UK will aim for ‘single set’ of global AI standards at G20
content:
NEW YORK — British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Tuesday an international agreement on AI led by the U.K. will seek to establish “a single set of global principles and standards.”

Burnham told a meeting with business leaders in New York that AI will be “the primary focus” of the U.K.’s upcoming G20 presidency.

It comes as discussions about global AI governance have shot up the diplomatic agenda, with Burnham telling journalists on his way to the United Nations General Assembly on Monday that the U.K. could be an “honest broker” for a global agreement on how to approach the technology.

It also came shortly before President Donald Trump used his address to the U.N. to assert that the United States “totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme” to control AI, in contrast to Burnham’s messaging.

“We want to pick up the initiatives that are beginning to emerge, develop, and bring them into a single set of global principles and standards that are very much about unlocking the full potential whilst guarding against the risks,” Burnham told businesses leaders on Tuesday.
snippet: NEW YORK — British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Tuesday an international agreement on AI led by the U.K. will seek to establish “a single set of global principles and standards.”
creator: Dan Bloom, Joseph Bambridge

title: EU lawmakers float product liability rules to help avert AI disaster
content:
BRUSSELS — European lawmakers are pushing to expand the EU’s flagship AI regulations to hold American tech companies liable for the risks their most advanced models pose to humanity, according to correspondence seen by POLITICO.

The proposal by four senior lawmakers in the European Parliament would add new rules to the EU’s landmark 2024 AI Act to ensure that companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic could be held liable when their technology is deployed in unforeseen ways.

The move shows Brussels is waking up to a reality in which AI-powered harm is already happening, and risks are multiplying — and marks the first concrete effort within the EU to respond to fears over AI safety that are dominating the global political agenda.

The group is calling on the Commission to introduce an AI Liability Act “to fill the legislative gaps currently existing for these kinds of incidents, so no people or European businesses are left empty-handed against these big providers when they cause harm,” according to a Sept. 16 note to the Commission seen by POLITICO.

title: 22 countries back call to keep AI ‘under human control’
content:
NEW YORK — Several European countries were among a group of 22 nations that adopted a declaration Monday saying that artificial intelligence “must remain under human direction, oversight and control” and suggesting to create a global supervisory regime.

The declaration, adopted on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly this week, acknowledged AI’s “potential to improve lives, advance science and strengthen our economies” but warned that “the rapid development of frontier AI models poses serious risks to safety and security if not appropriately managed.”

The push comes ahead of the meeting of U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, the leaders of the world’s leading AI-developing nations, in Washington Thursday.

Neither the U.S. nor China are part of the new declaration. But Finnish President Alexander Stubb, one of the main organizers of the document, told POLITICO that he hopes to create “momentum” and get more actors on board: “I think it will be in the interest of both China and the United States to have some kind of guardrails. And our message here is that we need human intervention, so humans need to be in charge,” he said in an interview.
snippet: NEW YORK — Several European countries were among a group of 22 nations that adopted a declaration Monday saying that artificial intelligence “must remain under human direction, oversight and control”
creator: Hans von der Burchard

title: EU pressures Big Tech to go green with new data center sustainability label
content:
BRUSSELS — Brussels on Monday unveiled an environmental rating scheme for data centers that power artificial intelligence, a move the EU’s energy chief described as the first step in pressuring tech giants into aligning with the continent’s climate efforts.

The new rules, which will apply from August 2027, oblige big data centers to display a label grading them on their energy efficiency, water usage and clean power uptake on a scale of A to G, much like the EU’s influential appliances ranking.

“This will add a lot of transparency and hopefully provide the incentives for these data centers to be as sustainable as possible,” said Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen in an interview with POLITICO ahead of the label’s presentation. 

The new label is optional for smaller data centers, “but later we are also going to introduce minimum performance standards which, of course, will put more pressure on those who may not voluntarily wish to be as sustainable as we want them to,” he added.

title: Google hit with €403M privacy fine over handling of user location data
content:
The Irish data privacy authority fined Google €403 million on Monday over how it has been gathering location data from users.

This is the fourth largest fine ever issued by the Irish regulator and its first major penalty against Google. Ireland is charged with enforcing the European Union’s privacy rules against many of the world’s tech giants that have their European headquarters in Ireland.

The decision concludes an inquiry that was opened in 2020 by the Irish Data Protection Commission (DPC), following complaints from consumer organizations across the EU over how Google processed people’s location data and the transparency around that processing. 

Google infringed the General Data Protection Regulation, the EU’s landmark laws, on four counts, said Ireland’s three privacy commissioners Des Hogan, Dale Sunderland and Niamh Sweeney. The issues concerned how Google processed and retained location data in its Web & App Activity, Location History and Location Accuracy functions, as well as transparency.

The complaints from consumer groups alleged that Google had used dark patterns and unfair practices to incite users to enable features that shared their location data.
snippet: The Irish data privacy authority fined Google €403 million on Monday over how it has been gathering location data from users.
creator: Ellen O'Regan, Eliza Gkritsi

title: EU budget needs taxes governments aren’t already raising, Costa says
content:
DUBLIN — Governments will be more likely to back new EU taxes for the bloc’s next seven-year budget if they raise money that national governments are not already collecting, European Council President António Costa said.

In an interview with POLITICO, Costa set out for the first time what he gathered from leaders during his tour of 25 capitals on one of the thorniest issues in the talks: how to build support towards new EU levies — known as “own resources” — that would generate fresh revenue to the budget.

The answer will help determine whether EU governments can agree on a budget by the end of the year — before 2027’s elections in France, Italy, Spain and Poland threaten to derail the talks — without either cutting spending on new priorities or asking national governments to pay more.

“If we don’t create new own resources, we need to ask [for] more money from the member states,” Costa said. “We know that we need to keep the national contributions at a reasonable limit. For this, we need to have a credible basket of new own resources.”
snippet: DUBLIN — Governments will be more likely to back new EU taxes for the bloc’s next seven-year budget if they raise money that national governments are not already collecting, European Council President
creator: Gregorio Sorgi

title: California’s Newsom signs executive order to explore new AI rules, consider ‘kill switch’
content:
California Gov. Gavin Newsom issued an executive order on Friday to speed up two AI laws he recently signed and explore proposals like requiring that AI companies develop a “kill switch” for their most advanced models.

The order comes after the Democrat told POLITICO this week he was mulling his options to take further action on AI safety, including a possible special legislative session to address recent safety concerns set off by AI researchers’ warnings that the technology could pose an existential risk to humanity and prominent autonomous hacking incidents.

Newsom said his executive action was also driven by federal inaction, after President Donald Trump responded to the warnings by dismissing them as a “hoax” and saying the only guardrails AI needs are his presidency. On Friday, Newsom urged Trump and Congress to adopt California’s AI framework or use the state’s existing regulations as a floor for federal rules.

“The federal government’s abject failure to create any form of meaningful AI oversight or accountability should alarm every American, especially when AI CEOs themselves are begging for regulation,” Newsom said in his press release.

title: The world wants to secure AI. It may have to try without the US.
content:
Global governments are struggling to find a path forward on AI without buy-in from the United States.

World leaders and tech CEOs are using the U.N. General Assembly this week to call for a global approach to rein in AI, particularly following cyberattacks against other technology firms in recent weeks. But that’s against the backdrop of President Donald Trump flatly rejecting in his own speech to the assembly any “globalist scheme of control” on AI.

That’s putting those countries that want to move forward in a tough spot.

“If the U.S. is not participating — where the U.S. has a lot of the labs — and also is not focusing on this as a policy matter, it limits their effectiveness,” said Christopher Painter, former cybersecurity coordinator at the State Department under both the Obama and Trump administrations.

That’s not to say they aren’t trying.

On Wednesday, the U.N. Security Council welcomed the heads of some of the U.S.’ top AI companies, who expressed their urgent fears about the future of securing these models, and called for international cooperation to confront these challenges.
snippet: Global governments are struggling to find a path forward on AI without buy-in from the United States.
creator: Maggie Miller

title: Don’t believe the doomers: Europe’s tech industry slams AI panic
content:
BRUSSELS — Amid fears that AI models could destroy humanity, top European tech leaders and cybersecurity experts have an increasingly loud response: Ignore the hype, and get on with the hard work of keeping the digital world safe.

That prosaic call is at the heart of an increasingly bitter backlash in Europe’s tech industry against the U.S.-generated panic about AI extinction. All the “Chicken Little” warnings, say both executives and cyber professionals, are getting in the way of the hard work of reinforcing defenses against the new AI reality.

The U.S. companies building the most advanced AI models have largely been responsible for raising the specter that artificial intelligence could lead to the demise of the human race. Fears have been peaking since incidents like OpenAI’s autonomous agents breaking into AI platform Hugging Face this summer, contributing to a warning earlier this month by former Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon that AI could soon “hack anything” and “kill us all.”

title: OpenAI model breaches Australian government websites
content:
OpenAI’s artificial intelligence models breached several Australian government websites earlier this year, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese disclosed Wednesday.

It’s the first publicly reported case of AI models autonomously hacking into government systems. There have been widespread calls from government officials and AI companies themselves for increased controls on AI frontier labs that have reported a series of incidents where they’ve lost control of their models.

“An artificial intelligence agent has infiltrated an Australian government website,” Albanese told reporters Wednesday on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York City.

Albanese said that the incident involved an “OpenAI agent gaining unauthorized access” in June to the Australian government’s Medicare statistics reporting portal, which is used to collect data on Medicare spending. While Albanese stressed that “no personal information is believed to have been accessed,” the agents did breach both public and non-public files on the site.
snippet: OpenAI’s artificial intelligence models breached several Australian government websites earlier this year, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese disclosed Wednesday.
creator: Maggie Miller

title: Rogue AI warnings are mostly ‘marketing,’ top European AI CEO says
content:
AMSTERDAM — The flurry of incidents in which AI agents went rogue and hacked other companies, and subsequent warnings of AI getting out of control, should be taken with a pinch of salt, a leading European AI boss told POLITICO.

“I think a lot of it is marketing, to overemphasize the proposed capabilities,” Max Junestrand, co-founder and CEO of Legora, an American-Swedish firm that develops collaborative AI tools for lawyers, said in an interview when asked about this summer’s AI hacking incidents.

As one of the continent’s top AI companies, Legora was valued at over $5 billion in its latest funding round earlier this year. The CEO’s comments echo a suggestion among some industry observers that frontier AI companies may have sought to benefit from the publicity around their models.

Yet Junestrand stressed that securing Legora’s operations against AI-fueled hacking attacks is a top priority, and emphasized that having access to the latest and most advanced models is key to doing that.
snippet: AMSTERDAM — The flurry of incidents in which AI agents went rogue and hacked other companies, and subsequent warnings of AI getting out of control, should be taken with a pinch of salt, a leading
creator: Pieter Haeck

title: Germany says Costa losing touch ‘with reality’ on EU budget
content:
BRUSSELS — Germany criticized European Council President António Costa on Tuesday over the fraught negotiations on the EU’s next seven-year budget.

Speaking on his way into a meeting of Europe ministers in Brussels, Germany’s Gunther Krichbaum said Costa’s recent interview with POLITICO was “not very helpful” and urged “more realism” on the budget.

In the interview, conducted in Dublin at the end of his budget tour of EU capitals, Costa said that agreeing to new EU-wide taxes, also known as own resources, is key to preventing major budget cuts and keeping national contributions to Brussels under control. He added that cuts to the Commission’s near-€2 trillion budget proposal risk running into opposition from many national governments.

However, Germany and allies from Northern Europe — whose contributions to the budget exceed their EU payouts — are pushing in the opposite direction, insisting that the EU slash its cashpot by hundreds of billions of euros. They argue that introducing new EU taxes is not an alternative to major cuts.

“One has to wonder whether Mr. Costa has completely lost touch with reality by now,” Krichbaum told reporters.
snippet: BRUSSELS — Germany criticized European Council President António Costa on Tuesday over the fraught negotiations on the EU’s next seven-year budget.
creator: Gregorio Sorgi, Nette Nöstlinger

title: UK seeks to broker global AI agreement at G20
content:
NEW YORK — The U.K. will seek to use its upcoming G20 presidency to forge a global agreement on AI, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said ahead of a visit to the U.N. General Assembly in New York.

This comes as discussions about global AI governance have shot up the diplomatic agenda in the wake of dire warnings about the potential threats from the technology, and marks the most significant intervention yet from the U.K.’s prime minister about how he will respond to perceived threats from AI.

Speaking to journalists on Monday night, Burnham said the U.K. is “uniquely positioned to play a leadership role on AI,” citing its relations with the EU, U.S. and China. He also said the U.K.’s expertise, including its AI Security Institute, means it could act as an “honest broker.”

“I think we can really do something in this space [that is] very significant,” Burnham said.

Burnham is due to meet Donald Trump for the first time as prime minister on Tuesday, and said he will assure the U.S. president that the U.K. will take a balanced approach on AI.
snippet: NEW YORK — The U.K. will seek to use its upcoming G20 presidency to forge a global agreement on AI, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said ahead of a visit to the U.N. General Assembly in New York.
creator: Dan Bloom, Joseph Bambridge

title: Friends with benefits: EU associate membership explained
content:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen surprised Brussels, and the world, during her 2026 State of the Union address by suggesting she wants to see Canada as an associate member of the EU.

European Parliament President Roberta Metsola, a Maltese member of von der Leyen’s center-right party, jumped on the idea. She suggested that Australia and New Zealand — which, like Malta and Canada, are Commonwealth countries — could also be candidates for the yet-to-be-defined category of EU associate membership.

While potentially attractive, the idea is neither simple nor well understood outside of EU policy circles. For now, it’s a political slogan only.

The closest existing model is the European Economic Area, in which Norway, Iceland and tiny Liechtenstein participate, as a way of accessing Europe’s single market and regulatory space.

Here, POLITICO explains why it’s so hard to get close to EU membership, and what rights and obligations would flow from any country pursuing such a deep set of ties:

Ursula von der Leyen’s proposal is best understood as an invitation to design a new arrangement for deeper relations between the EU and its trusted partners.
snippet: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen surprised Brussels, and the world, during her 2026 State of the Union address by suggesting she wants to see Canada as an associate member of the EU.
creator: Ryan Heath

title: AI titans invited to Trump-Xi dinner
content:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon plan to attend next week’s state dinner with President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping, four people familiar with the event told POLITICO.

The executives’ attendance at the White House summit signals artificial intelligence will likely be a key talking point during negotiations and comes as fear the technology could destroy humanity has roiled the industry.

An OpenAI spokesperson, who confirmed Altman’s attendance, did not detail his goals for the summit and instead pointed to his recent comments that the two leaders could earn a Nobel Peace Prize if they reach a deal on AI. Another person, who was granted anonymity to speak on details not yet made public, confirmed Huang’s attendance, but did not provide details on his goals for the summit.

Amon, whose attendance was confirmed by a Qualcomm spokesperson, said the CEO will represent the company and “the strength of American technology leadership on the global stage.”

Anthropic declined to comment on whether it received an invitation. Spokespeople for Google, Meta and AMD did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
snippet: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon plan to attend next week’s state dinner with President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping, four people familiar
creator: Katherine Long

title: Parents, privacy, parliaments: The battle begins for von der Leyen’s social media ban
content:
BRUSSELS — Ursula von der Leyen’s bill to keep young Europeans off social media is an ambitious response to the growing outcry over the potential harm of TikTok, Instagram and other online platforms. Making the restrictions a reality will require a whole new level of ambition.

The European Commission must now negotiate with national governments and technologists to figure out exactly how to impose a law across Europe that would ban kids under 13 from social media, and severely restrict access for those under 15 — all without trampling on privacy of young and old alike in the process of verifying users’ age. 

Reducing the harms of social media on youth has been a top priority for the Commission president, a medical doctor and mother of seven who has repeatedly decried the internet’s impact on the health of minors since her 2025 State of the Union speech.  

“If a platform wants to access the children or the teenagers, the minors, they have to prove first that they are safe,” she told reporters on Thursday as she officially unveiled the EU Kids Act, the day after again touting her leadership on the issue in this year’s annual address.
snippet: BRUSSELS — Ursula von der Leyen’s bill to keep young Europeans off social media is an ambitious response to the growing outcry over the potential harm of TikTok, Instagram and other online platforms.
creator: Eliza Gkritsi, Ellen O'Regan

title: AI king Jensen Huang pushes ‘responsible optimism’ at King Charles III’s gathering
content:
AYRSHIRE, Scotland — King Charles relied on all his pulling power to bring together some of the most powerful people in the world of AI to a rural corner of Scotland. 

Preparations for Thursday’s event at the 18th century estate of Dumfries House, first reported by POLITICO, had been in the works for months in close communication with the U.K. government.

But the significance of the event intensified in recent weeks after a series of alarming incidents of AI agents escaping their testing environments to hack other firms, and warnings from those in the industry that humanity’s very existence could be under threat.  

For the first time since worries about AI eradicating humanity sparked a wave of calls for immediate regulation, the companies were all under one roof. Charles addressed the dire warnings in his remarks to his guests. 

“There seems urgency in adequately considering the existential dangers of such technologies falling into the wrong hands and being used in potentially catastrophic ways,” he said. “Surely, then, we need sufficient means of control before it is all too late.”
snippet: AYRSHIRE, Scotland — King Charles relied on all his pulling power to bring together some of the most powerful people in the world of AI to a rural corner of Scotland.
creator: Joseph Bambridge

title: European Investment Bank chief heads to Ottawa amid warming EU-Canada ties
content:
European Investment Bank President Nadia Calviño is heading to Ottawa on Sunday to lay the groundwork for Europe-Canada cooperation on critical raw materials, an official from her office said.

Calviño will be meeting with government officials including Canada’s minister for energy and natural resources, Tim Hodgson, in Ottawa.

The aim of her visit is for the European Investment Bank, the long-term lending arm of the European Union, to establish a presence in Canada and begin operations “as soon as the administrative paperwork is done, with a focus on [critical raw materials],” the official said. They were granted anonymity to speak about the internal strategy.

Coming after European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Wednesday proposed admitting Canada as an associate member of the EU, Calviño’s trip is significant given that the EIB typically only operates in developing countries or members of the European Union or European Economic Area.

Ahead of this year’s G7 summit, Canada extended a behind-the-scenes offer to alliance members for “priority access” to its critical minerals stockpile, according to a letter seen by POLITICO from Hodgson.
snippet: European Investment Bank President Nadia Calviño is heading to Ottawa on Sunday to lay the groundwork for Europe-Canada cooperation on critical raw materials, an official from her office said.
creator: Nicholas Vinocur

title: Jensen Huang: Don’t regulate AI like social media
content:
AYRSHIRE, SCOTLAND — Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said AI should not be regulated like social media because AI is a “technology” rather than a “product.”

Speaking at an AI event convened by King Charles III at Dumfries House in Ayrshire, Scotland, Huang told journalists that AI is “very different than social media” and that at present the security issues involving AI are “related to products not ready to be released.”

His remarks come as governments around the world are grappling with whether to place regulatory constraints on AI, and after AI executives, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, have called for a slowing of AI development.

“Unlike social media, which is a product, AI is a technology that’s behind all of these other tech, all of these products — and so, regulate the products,” Huang said.

He said authorities should monitor for when an AI deployment “goes wrong” and “whenever new laws are necessary, add to the existing laws,” but pointed out that there are existing regulations in sectors where AI is deployed such healthcare, transportation, and entertainment.

title: Canada’s Carney stops short of endorsing von der Leyen’s associate member plan
content:
STRASBOURG — Mark Carney used an address to the European Parliament to sketch out what Ottawa would want from closer ties with the EU but declined to give full-throated approval of Ursula von der Leyen’s surprise “associate member” plan.

Speaking a day after the Commission president floated the unique relationship status, the Canadian prime minister acknowledged the offer and instead of accepting it outright, listed potential individual areas of cooperation, including critical minerals, defense, AI, energy security, and space.

He also called for more seamless digital trade in non-agricultural goods and services, as well as Canadian participation in Erasmus+, the EU’s student exchange program.

“We welcome this ambition,” he said, after name-checking the idea of von der Leyen, who was sitting in the audience. “Polling shows an overwhelming majority of Canadians support much closer ties.”

Carney’s list of potential tie-ups was an early attempt to put substance behind what, for now, remains a largely undefined political proposition.
